contracts.summary: Counts analytical nodes with assigned supports.
contracts.remarks: When to use: This is the supported-node count used by GetSupportedNodeIds, not the number of distinct support definitions or any contiguous ID range. Zero is valid data. Exact nonnegative integral returns are required; Boolean success is never treated as count one. No node geometry is hydrated.

contracts.summary: Reads an owned bounded snapshot of supported analytical node IDs.
contracts.remarks: When to use: Use for node discovery instead of enumerating support-definition IDs from a count. The native return is a count, not a Boolean flag; -1 is failure. Count/list/count must agree; a changed count returns StateChanged with no payload and no retry. Zero is rechecked and returns an owned empty list without native list invocation. Initialized Int32 arrays must be completely written; native order and duplicates remain unchanged. Equal counts cannot prove an atomic model snapshot.

contracts.summary: Reads the native support type assigned to one analytical node.
contracts.remarks: When to use: Prefer this inexpensive type-only observation when DOF states and stiffnesses are not needed. Native 0 is successful NoSupport data; -1 is NativeFailure. Unknown nonnegative codes retain NativeTypeCode and KnownType=null, without being cast to a fabricated known enum. GetSupportInformation instead requires a reviewed type and written six-DOF buffers. The metadata input is passed by value despite a mutable-reference help declaration.

contracts.summary: Reads six native support DOF states and spring constants at one node.
contracts.remarks: When to use: Unlike GetSupportType, this retrieves all FX/FY/FZ/MX/MY/MZ restraint observations. The native return is a support-type code, never a Boolean success flag. Type 0 yields NoSupport without consuming untouched buffers; -1 yields NativeFailure; an unknown positive type yields UnsupportedNativeType without guessing its layout. Known positive types require six written Int32 states (-1 spring, 0 fixed, 1 released) and six finite nonnegative floating-point stiffnesses. Springs are not collapsed to released=true. Native local support axes, force/length translational stiffness and moment/angle rotational stiffness are retained without conversion.

contracts.summary: Reads a support item’s GUID as parsed and exact native text.
contracts.remarks: When to use: This takes a support item/definition ID, not a node number, support-list index or user-facing name. Null, DBNull or empty native text gives EmptyOrUnavailable; malformed GUID text throws. Exact native text and parsed Guid are both retained. Guid.Empty, if returned, remains an observed value, not a generated replacement. SetSupportUniqueId writes a new identity and has only void invocation evidence.

When to use: This is a definition count, not supported-node count, assignment count or maximum support ID. Use GetElasticMat with a known positive definition ID; there is no inferred 1..count discovery. Zero is valid integral data. Plate-mat and footing definition counts are separate queries.

contracts.summary: Reads one elastic-mat definition’s native parameters and assigned-node count.
contracts.remarks: When to use: Use a known support definition ID, not a node ID or zero-based index. Native true qualifies direction 0..5, scalar subgrade, print flag, spring-generation type and nonnegative assignment count; false exposes no default packet. This query does not read assigned nodes; GetElasticMatAssignedNodeIds performs a bounded detail/list/detail observation. Native subgrade is force/length cubed, not force/length nodal stiffness. Only direction variants and compression/multilinear generation remain distinct. No model or geometry objects are hydrated.

contracts.summary: Reads owned node assignments for one explicit elastic-mat definition.
contracts.remarks: When to use: The returned IDs are analytical nodes, never plate IDs or support-definition IDs. Allocation uses qualified GetElasticMat detail, then Boolean list retrieval and a complete detail recheck. Exceeding maximumResults gives LimitExceeded before list allocation; zero assignments return an owned empty list after recheck. Changed count/direction/subgrade/flags gives StateChanged without payload or retry. Native order/duplicates are preserved; equal metadata does not detect every same-count edit.

When to use: This count concerns plate-mat definitions, not plates, support nodes, assigned entities or maximum support reference. Zero is valid integral data. It does not resolve plate-mat ID/index or scalar/array contract gates; no plate assignments or subgrades are synthesized from this count.

When to use: This is independent of the supported-node and elastic-mat counts. No documented footing index-to-ID enumeration is assumed; supply known support IDs to GetElasticFooting. Zero is valid, and a count is never decoded as a success flag.

contracts.summary: Reads an existing elastic-footing definition’s geometry, direction, soil modulus and assignment count.
contracts.remarks: When to use: Unlike GetElasticMat, the native footing packet includes finite positive length and width as well as native direction 0..5, scalar subgrade and assigned-node count. Known support definition ID is required. Native 1/true succeeds, 0/false fails; integral -1 is not VARIANT_TRUE for this narrower contract. Lengths remain native length units and subgrade remains force/length cubed; no area, spring stiffness or reaction is derived.

contracts.summary: Reads owned node assignments of one explicit elastic-footing definition.
contracts.remarks: When to use: Uses qualified footing detail/list/detail, retaining node identity and every observed length/width/direction/modulus/count in its state check. Native 1/true is success; 0/false is failure and numeric -1 is rejected rather than treated as true. Empty assignment is a rechecked owned empty list. LimitExceeded occurs before list allocation. StateChanged has no payload; same-count edits can remain undetected, so coordinate session access. No node geometry is hydrated or reordered.

contracts.summary: Creates a native fixed-support definition without assigning it.
contracts.remarks: When to use: This creates a support definition and returns its qualified positive reference; it does not attach it to nodes. AssignSupportToNodes is a separate mutation. Native -1 is failure; Boolean success or native zero is not accepted as a created reference. No mutable managed support ID is overwritten. Read back assignments separately before drawing restraint/engineering conclusions.

contracts.summary: Creates the native pinned-support definition without inventing its restraint packet.
contracts.remarks: When to use: The native pinned operation is separate from synthesizing fixed-but release flags. Help describes local Y/Z rotations while the private source convenience releases all rotations; this method deliberately returns only the created ID and does not claim torsional restraint. Assign it separately, then use GetSupportInformation at a node to observe actual states. Native -1 is failure; success requires a positive integral reference.

contracts.summary: Creates a native fixed-but support from an owned explicit release/stiffness definition.
contracts.remarks: When to use: Use when creation flags and springs must be specified explicitly rather than using the dedicated fixed/pinned calls. FixedButSupportDefinition snapshots the existing Releases/Springs packets. Native input flags are six Double 0/1 values, not the read-back Spring=-1 state or member partial-release modes. Native arrays are fresh copies; the caller’s packets are not changed. Stiffness units and release/spring interaction remain native semantics without scaling or inferred modes. Native -1 fails; a positive integral support ID is required.

contracts.parameters: int supportId, IEnumerable<int> nodeIds, int maximumResults = 100000
contracts.summary: Assigns an existing support definition to an owned explicit analytical-node selection.
contracts.remarks: When to use: Creation and assignment are separate; this function sends one Int32 node-ID array to native AssignSupportToNode in node-array-first/support-ID-second order. The support ID must be appropriate for node assignment; this is not the plate-mat entity-list route. Input is enumerated once and bounded; order and duplicates remain unchanged. Integral 0 is success and -1 is failure; actual Boolean false is not numeric zero-success. Empty input produces NoOperation after binding checks and no native invocation. No per-node acknowledgement is invented; partial native effects on failure are possible.
contracts.signature: SupportMutationResult AssignSupportToNodes(int supportId, IEnumerable<int> nodeIds, int maximumResults = 100000)

contracts.summary: Removes a support assignment from one analytical node.
contracts.remarks: When to use: This unassigns one node; DeleteSupport removes a shared definition and its assignments. Native 1/true is success, 0/false is failure. Failure does not prove that no support existed. No shared definition deletion, family-specific fallback, retry, save or managed node update is performed.

contracts.summary: Deletes a support definition and its native assignments.
contracts.remarks: When to use: This is broader than RemoveSupportFromNode, which targets only one assignment. The documented operation removes the support item and its assignments; the request retains the support ID without pretending to know every affected node. Integral 0 is success and -1 is failure; Boolean false is not decoded as numeric zero. Native partial changes may remain on failure and cannot be rolled back by this result.

contracts.summary: Invokes the native void setter for one support item’s GUID.
contracts.remarks: When to use: This writes a nonempty explicitly supplied Guid to a support definition/item, not a node. GetSupportUniqueId reads its actual current value. The native setter returns void, so completed dispatch produces InvokedWithoutAcknowledgement and IsSuccessful=false, with the requested ID/GUID retained and no fabricated native flag. No automatic read-back or persistence claim occurs; callers may request a separate read-back if needed. The Guid is marshaled as canonical D-format text.
